question: to the Commission Johan Danielsson (S&D) Subject:

In the light of recent disruptions in the Middle East, there is a need to assess the EU’s preparedness regarding the availability of aviation fuel. Air transport is critical both for the functioning of the internal market and for crisis response. At the same time, the EU remains highly dependent on imports of aviation fuels from non-EU countries. In parallel, the EU has set ambitious targets for the uptake of sustainable aviation fuels, notably through the ReFuelEU Aviation Regulation1. However, implementation remains slow and production capacity within the EU is still limited, which risks delaying both the green transition and efforts to strengthen resilience. Against this background: 1.

Does the Commission intend to propose EU-wide requirements for minimum aviation fuel stock levels, in particular at major airports and strategic transport hubs, in order to strengthen preparedness and resilience in times of crisis?

What concrete measures will the Commission take to accelerate the build-up of sustainable aviation fuel production capacity within the EU and ensure that Member States meet their obligations under the ReFuelEU Aviation Regulation?

Regulation (EU) 2023/2405 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 October 2023 on ensuring a level playing field for sustainable air transport (ReFuelEU Aviation) (OJ L, 2023/2405, 31.10.2023, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/2405/oj).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.6.2026) In response to the impact of the Middle East crisis, the Commission announced the launch of a revision process for the Oil Stockholding Directive in its AccelerateEU communication1. One of the objectives of the revision is to address the challenges identified in the current crisis, considering among others whether specific stock requirements are needed for different oil products, adaptations for sustainable fuels, mitigation of emerging risks, and enhanced military mobility readiness through improved energy resilience. The Commission has also published guidance clarifying certain EU rules applicable to passengers and tourism as well as transport operators, including in light of the current reduced supply of jet fuel from the Middle East2. The Sustainable Transport Investment Plan3 aims to accelerate investment in sustainable aviation fuels (SAF) in the EU and reaffirms the commitment to ReFuelEU Aviation4 implementation. The Plan includes actions on the Commission to work with Member States to set up a pooled joint double-sided auction for synthetic aviation fuels (eSAF), while simultaneously providing valuable insights in view of establishing an EU-wide financing mechanism. To this end, the Commission launched eSAF Early Movers Coalition in December 20255 and launched a study to define auctions design and governance. Member States are responsible for enforcing the application of ReFuelEU Aviation through their respective competent authorities and imposing fines in case of non-compliance by aviation fuel suppliers, aircraft operators and EU airport managing bodies.
